title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
authors: Yiyi Cai, Yongtao Zhan, Alexander Zlokapa
abstract: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model is a strongly interacting fermionic system. Its dynamics are difficult to analyze with Lieb-Robinson bounds and cluster expansions due to its all-to-all disordered interactions. We prove that, with high probability over the disorder, the SYK model admits a quantum Gibbs sampler with a system-size-independent spectral gap at sufficiently high constant temperatures. This yields polynomial-time preparation of SYK Gibbs states on a quantum computer. While prior non-rigorous computations that suggested SYK thermalization were limited to studying local correlators, we emphasize that our result holds up to arbitrary inverse polynomial trace distance. Our proof introduces the pseudo-Lindbladian approach to fermions and uses an especially simple SYK analysis based on a comparison to classical dynamics.
summary: This work rigorously proves that the highly interacting SYK model exhibits fast thermalization at high temperatures. By comparing the quantum evolution dynamics to a simpler classical mean-field model, the authors establish a spectral gap, which guarantees that the model's equilibrium state can be prepared efficiently on a quantum computer.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the fast mixing of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model at high temperatures to establish a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for preparing its Gibbs states.
main_result: The authors prove fast mixing with high probability over the disorder, implying that the SYK Gibbs state can be prepared in polynomial time on a quantum computer up to arbitrary inverse polynomial trace distance.
method: The proof employs a pseudo-Lindbladian approach for fermions and crucially compares the quantum Jacobian of the dynamics to a classical Jacobian derived from a commuting variable mean-field model.
model_or_system: The system is the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, a strongly interacting fermionic system characterized by an all-to-all quartic interaction Hamiltonian involving Majorana fermions. The dynamics are analyzed via a Lindbladian construction satisfying KMS detailed balance.
key_observables: Spectral Gap, Quantum and Classical Jacobians ($D_\gamma$ and $D_x$), and the mixing time $t_{	ext{mix}}(\epsilon)$.
important_parameters: High constant temperature regime ($ eta \le 1/(1000J)$), system size $N$, and disorder strength $J$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on bounding the quantum Jacobian by a classical one, and the mathematical rigor involves advanced tools like Banach's theorem and Borell-TIS inequalities.
paper_structure: The paper develops the analysis by first defining the quantum and classical dynamics, then establishing the core comparison between their respective Jacobians, and finally using advanced concentration inequalities to bound the required norms.
why_interesting: The rigorous proof of fast thermalization in a complex, strongly interacting model like SYK, using techniques that bridge quantum dynamics to classical mean-field theory, is highly relevant for understanding quantum thermalization dynamics.
